questions.q: What is a semantic model, in the context of this lesson?
options: The modeling layer between the warehouse and the report, where data is related and measures are defined
A synonym for the bronze layer of a data lake
A type of SQL Server transaction log
A file format used only for CSV extracts
questions.explain: A semantic model — a Power BI dataset, a Tableau data source, an AAS model — sits between the warehouse and the report, adding relationships and measures.

questions.q: Why does a measure represent a genuinely different kind of lineage edge compared to a warehouse column?
options: A measure can be built from a column, another measure, or several measures combined, creating branching lineage that table-to-table chains don't have
Measures never have any upstream dependency at all
Measures are always identical to warehouse columns
Measures only exist in data lakes, never in semantic models
questions.explain: Unlike a column with one clear upstream source, a measure can reference other measures, letting lineage inside the model branch and recombine.

questions.q: What's the key lineage tradeoff of Import mode versus DirectQuery?
options: Import copies data at refresh time (fast, but frozen); DirectQuery queries live (current, but inherits upstream freshness issues)
DirectQuery is always slower and less accurate than Import
Import mode cannot be used with any warehouse
There is no lineage difference between the two modes
questions.explain: Import mode freezes data as of the last refresh; DirectQuery stays current but passes through whatever freshness state the warehouse is already in.

questions.q: In the measure-to-measure lineage example, what does '[Total Sales YoY]' depend on?
options: The '[Total Sales]' measure, which itself depends on the fact_sales.amount column
Nothing — it is calculated independently with no upstream dependency
Only the visual it appears on
A separate warehouse table unrelated to Total Sales
questions.explain: The chain shown is fact_sales.amount feeding the base [Total Sales] measure, which in turn feeds [Total Sales YoY] — a measure built on a measure.

questions.q: Why does knowing whether 'wrong' means 'stale' or 'live' matter for a semantic model?
options: It tells you whether the problem is a frozen Import-mode refresh or a real-time upstream issue coming through DirectQuery
It determines which chart type the report should use
It has no practical effect on troubleshooting
It only matters for choosing a color palette
questions.explain: Import mode freezes data as of last refresh, so a 'wrong' number might just be stale; DirectQuery means the number reflects whatever is happening upstream right now.
